title: BILL ACKMAN'S PERSHING SQUARE JUST UPDATED ITS STOCK PORTFOLIO
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
Ackman put about $2.0B into two new names — $1.01B of exchange  
operator Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) and $954M of eye-care company  
Alcon (ALC) — and added 17.82% to Netflix (NFLX). The sharper move is  
what he took off: Microsoft (MSFT) was cut 34.51%, with trims to Meta  
(META), Mastercard (MA), Visa (V), Brookfield (BN) and Restaurant  
Brands (QSR), and a full exit from Hertz (HTZ).  
  
This is everything they owned as of the end of Q3:  
  
\- $10.3B of Pershing Square (PS)  
\- $2.35B of Uber (UBER)  
\- $2.12B of Amazon (AMZN)  
\- $2.08B of Microsoft (MSFT) (cut 34.51%)  
\- $2.05B of Meta (META) (cut 11.35%)  
\- $2.05B of Howard Hughes (HHH)  
\- $1.87B of Brookfield (BN) (cut 10.70%)  
\- $1.56B of Restaurant Brands (QSR) (cut 14.77%)  
\- $1.07B of Netflix (NFLX) (added 17.82%)  
\- $1.04B of Mastercard (MA) (cut 11.12%)  
\- $1.03B of Visa (V) (cut 12.22%)  
\- $1.02B of S&P Global (SPGI)  
\- $1.01B of Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) (new)  
\- $954M of Alcon (ALC) (new)  
\- $148M of Pershing Square USA (PSUS)  
\- $115M of Seaport Entertainment (SEG)  
  
Sold out: Hertz (HTZ)  
  
Holdings are as of September 30, per Pershing Square's Q3 13F filing.  
13Fs only cover long U.S.-listed positions and lag the market, so the  
fund may have changed these since then. The PS line is Pershing  
Square's own listed shares; the share count was unchanged from a Q2  
amendment filed the same day as this 13F.  
  
Would love to hear how people read the ICE and Alcon entries versus  
the Microsoft cut — which move feels more important?
